question: Looking back at your completed task, how did you decide what to read or request next, and when you had enough information to answer? Give a brief account of observable choices and the information you expected further reads to provide.
answer: I first used discovery to find the package-query guidance. The narrow discovery result exposed dependency facets but not the full query syntax, so I made a broader discovery request and read the query-space resource. I inspected its binding and dependency facet rules to choose a bounded Microsoft.Extensions.* search with depends=Polly and dependency-target=net10.0. The search returned Microsoft.Extensions.Http.Polly 10.0.12, the selected .NETStandard2.0 group for net10.0, and its direct Polly 7.2.4 declaration. It also reported CandidateLimitReached at 40/40, so I could answer with one package and explicitly say the family was not exhausted. I stopped there because inspecting the returned package would only recheck facts already present; additional searches could find more packages but were not needed for the up-to-three answer and would add latency.
